This relationship is supported by the presence of Dacarbazine, which is a member of the alkylating activity class and directly interacts with Cyp2e1. The lowest common ancestor of Streptozocin and Dacarbazine is the organooxygen compound, indicating a shared biochemical pathway. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential mechanism by which Streptozocin may influence Cyp2e1 activity, possibly through the induction of metabolic pathways that involve cytochrome P450 enzymes. This connection underscores the role of Cyp2e1 in the metabolic processing of alkylating agents, suggesting a possible link between Streptozocin and Cyp2e1 in the context of drug metabolism.
